name: SnapDock
summary: A Mac or Windows style dock for Omarchy, with Launchpad, Shortcuts, Task Manager and Windows-style window snapping
description:
New in 2.0: rebuilt from scratch. Pick a Mac, Windows or SnapDock dock, open every app from a Mac-style Launchpad, end stuck apps in Task Manager. Full list under What's New below.

SnapDock gives Omarchy a beautiful dock and makes your desktop feel instantly familiar if you're coming from a Mac or Windows.

YOUR DOCK, YOUR STYLE
- Mac: a floating glass shelf, icons that grow as your mouse passes, a dot under open apps.
- Windows: a taskbar across the bottom with a Start button.
- SnapDock: a glass pill with a soft shine.
Switch any time at the bottom of SnapDock Settings. Small, medium or large, and auto-hide that slides away like on a Mac.

EVERYTHING ONE CLICK AWAY
- Click an app to open it, click again to minimize it, click a minimized app to bring it back.
- Right-click any app: its windows, new window, minimize, maximize, snap layouts, move to desktop 1-5, keep in dock, Close and Force quit.
- Menus and SnapDock Settings close by themselves when you move the mouse away.
- Point at an open app to see live previews of its windows.
- Unlock the dock and drag icons wherever you want them.

LAUNCHPAD
All apps opens a full-screen grid of every app on your computer, like a Mac. Type to search, press Enter to open. Prefer Omarchy's own menu? Switch it in Settings.

SHORTCUTS
YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Discord, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Spotify, Netflix, Gmail and many more, each opening in its own window. Switch each one on or off.

TASK MANAGER
Ctrl + Shift + Esc, just like Windows. See what each app is using, then End task or Force quit anything that's stuck.

WINDOWS THAT SNAP
Drag a window to a screen edge or corner to snap it. Super + arrows snap and maximize; Super + Z and the title bar give you snap layouts. Drag a window to the desktop numbers at the top left to move it there.

SCREENSHOTS AND SCREEN RECORDING
Click the camera on the dock and pick an area, a window, the whole screen, or the whole screen in 3 seconds. Right-click it for the whole screen straight away. Copied and saved in Pictures. Switch to Record to film the whole screen or an area, with sound; click the red dot on the camera to stop.

AND MORE
Show desktop (Super + D), a screensaver button that locks your computer, Live TV with free public channels, a Trash on the dock, minimize and maximize buttons on every title bar (browsers too), and new glossy icons.

SAFE BY DESIGN
SnapDock 2 never edits your own settings files. It adds one line to Hyprland's settings and takes it out again if you remove it. Coming from an older SnapDock? Everything the old version changed is put back first.

Free for a limited time, and early adopters get free updates for life.

featured.headline: Your dock. Mac or Windows style.
featured.tagline: SnapDock 2 is rebuilt from scratch: a Mac, Windows or SnapDock dock, a Mac-style Launchpad, Shortcuts for your favourite sites, a Task Manager to end stuck apps, and Windows-style snapping. It never touches your own settings. Free for a limited time, and early adopters get free updates for life.
featured.launch_offer: Free for a limited time · early adopters get free updates for life

features.title: Mac, Windows or SnapDock style
features.body: Pick the dock you know: a floating Mac shelf whose icons grow under your mouse, a Windows taskbar with a Start button, or SnapDock's own glass pill. Switch any time at the bottom of SnapDock Settings.

features.title: Launchpad
features.body: All apps opens a full-screen grid of every app, like a Mac. Type to search and press Enter to open. Right-click an app to keep it in the dock. Prefer Omarchy's menu? It's one switch.

features.title: Task Manager
features.body: Ctrl + Shift + Esc, just like Windows. See how much each app uses, then End task or Force quit anything that stopped responding.

features.title: Shortcuts
features.body: YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Discord, Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Spotify, Netflix, Gmail and many more, each opening in its own window. Turn each one on or off.

features.title: Move your icons
features.body: Unlock the dock and drag icons wherever you want them, apps and shortcuts alike. Lock it again when you're done.

features.title: Close and Force quit
features.body: Right-click any open app to close it, or force quit it if it's frozen. Menus close by themselves when you move the mouse away.

features.title: Window previews
features.body: Point at an open app on the dock to see live pictures of its windows. Click one to bring it forward, or close it from there.

features.title: Screensaver and lock
features.body: One click on the moon starts the screensaver and locks the computer, so it asks for your password when you come back.

features.title: Screenshots and screen recording
features.body: The camera on the dock takes an area, a window, the whole screen, or the whole screen in 3 seconds. Switch to Record to film the whole screen or an area, with the computer's sound and your microphone. Click the red dot to stop.

features.title: Show desktop
features.body: Super + D, or the button on the dock, sends every window down so you see your background. Press again and they all come back.

features.title: Never touches your files
features.body: SnapDock 2 only adds one line to Hyprland's settings and removes it again if you uninstall. Upgrading from an older SnapDock puts back everything it changed.

features.title: Minimize, like Windows
features.body: The — button on any title bar hides the window and keeps its icon in the dock. Click the icon and it comes back exactly where it was. Super + Down minimizes too.

features.title: Move to another desktop
features.body: Send a window to desktop 1–5 (the numbers at the top left): click ⧉ on its title bar and pick a number, or drag it to the top left corner and drop it on a numbered tile.

features.title: Snap layouts
features.body: Halves, quarters, thirds, two-thirds, fill and centre. Super + Z or the ⊞ button shows them all.

features.title: Drag to snap
features.body: Drag a window to an edge or corner. A see-through preview shows where it'll land.

features.title: Snap Assist
features.body: Snap one window and pick what fills the rest of the screen, just like Windows.

features.title: Smart title bars
features.body: Desktops ⧉, snap layouts ⊞, minimize —, maximize □ and close ✕ on every title bar. Double-click to maximize or restore.

features.title: Resize from any edge
features.body: Grab any window edge with the mouse, snapped windows included.

features.title: Speaks your language
features.body: 33 languages, picked automatically from your computer's language. Choose another one any time: SnapDock → Language.

steps.title: Install it
steps.body: Press GET in the Omarchy Store app, or use one of the install options above. Type your password when asked.

steps.title: It sets itself up
steps.body: SnapDock appears at the bottom of your screen by itself. Coming from an older SnapDock? It puts back everything the old one changed first.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.body: Click the gear on the dock: pick Mac, Windows or SnapDock style at the bottom, the size, Shortcuts, and unlock the dock to move icons.

shortcuts.does: Task Manager: see what's running, End task or Force quit
Launchpad: every app in a full-screen grid, type to search
Show desktop; press again to bring the windows back
Screenshot: pick an area (or click a window)
Snap to the left half (press again from the right half to go to a quarter)
Fill the screen, or from a half, snap to the top quarter
Put the window back, or from a half, snap to the bottom quarter. On a window that isn't snapped: minimize
Show every snap layout for the current window
Minimize; click the app's dock icon to bring it back
Move the window to desktop 1–5 (click a number or type it)
Drop the window on a numbered tile to move it to that desktop
Left/right edge: half · corner: quarter · top: fill

faq.a: Right now, yes, for a limited time. SnapDock becomes a paid app after launch. Everyone who gets it while it's free is an early adopter and gets every future update free, for life.

faq.q: Does it work with my theme?
faq.a: Yes. The dock and title bars recolour themselves whenever you switch Omarchy themes.

faq.q: Will it mess up my setup?
faq.a: No. SnapDock 2 never edits your own settings files. It adds one line to Hyprland's settings and keeps everything else in its own folders. Coming from an older SnapDock? It first puts back everything the old version changed.

faq.q: How do I switch between Mac and Windows style?
faq.a: Click the gear on the dock (SnapDock Settings). Dock style is at the bottom: Mac, Windows or SnapDock. It changes right away.

faq.q: How do I move the icons on the dock?
faq.a: Right-click the dock and choose Unlock to move icons (or use the switch in SnapDock Settings). The icons wiggle: drag them where you want them, then lock the dock again.

faq.q: An app froze. How do I close it?
faq.a: Right-click its icon on the dock and choose Force quit. Or press Ctrl + Shift + Esc for the Task Manager, pick the app and press Force quit.

faq.q: Where does a minimized window go?
faq.a: It waits out of sight, and its icon stays in the dock. Click the icon and it comes back on the desktop it came from, in the same spot. To bring every minimized window back at once: SnapDock → Snap layouts → Bring back all minimized windows.

The numbers at the top left of Omarchy are separate desktops, each with its own windows (like Task View desktops on Windows). Click a number to switch to it. SnapDock lets you send a window to one: ⧉ on the title bar, or drag the window onto the tiles that appear at the top left.

faq.q: Something isn't working. What do I do?
faq.a: Open a terminal and type snapdock doctor. It checks the usual causes (another dock running, a settings error, a missing program) and tells you what to do.
The Omarchy Store's Updates tab shows new versions: press UPDATE.
Press Remove on SnapDock's page in the Omarchy Store. Or open a terminal and type snapdock uninstall. It takes out its one line and its own files, and your setup is exactly as it was.
A recent Omarchy (version 4 or newer). On older versions SnapDock tells you to update Omarchy first and changes nothing.

promise.title: Free for a limited time. Early adopters get free updates for life.
promise.body: SnapDock is free right now, but not forever: it becomes a paid app after launch. Get it while it's free and you're an early adopter: every future update is included at no cost, for life.

install.note: Already have an older SnapDock, or a dock setup of your own? SnapDock 2 puts back whatever the old version changed and never edits your own files.

featured.new_line: New in 2.0.6: the dock's Omarchy Store button opens the new Omarchy Store app, with its own logo.

changelog.title: Works with the new Omarchy Store app
items: The Omarchy Store button on the dock opens the new Omarchy Store app, with the store's own logo.
If you still have the older store app, the button keeps working with that one too.

changelog.title: Logos update by themselves
items: When an app gets a new logo (from an update or the store), SnapDock shows it within a couple of seconds. No restart, no log out.
This works for the dock, Launchpad, the menus and the TV button (Rabbit Ears).
Apps installed while SnapDock is running get their proper logo straight away too.

changelog.title: Screen recording, with sound
items: Screen recording: click the camera on the dock, choose Record, then Whole screen or Area.
Record the computer's sound, your microphone, or both. Two switches right in the card.
While it records, the camera shows a red dot. Click it to stop. The video is saved in Videos and a preview pops up.
Right-click the camera for Record the whole screen, Record an area, or Stop recording.
The app names above the dock icons are no longer cut off at the top.

changelog.title: The Power button is back
items: A red Power button on the dock: click it to restart the computer (it asks first, so nothing happens by accident).
Right-click the Power button for Restart, Shut down, Lock, Log out, or Omarchy's own power menu.
Restart and Shut down use Omarchy's own commands, so your apps close properly first.
You can hide the button in SnapDock Settings (Power button).

changelog.title: Every window gets the buttons
items: Files, Telegram, browsers and every other app now get the same title bar: desktops, snap layouts, minimize, maximize and close. Before, some apps (like Files) had no bar, so those buttons were missing.
Drag-to-snap and moving windows to another desktop work in every app too.

changelog.title: The TV button opens Rabbit Ears itself
items: The TV button on the dock now opens the real Rabbit Ears app when you have it, so every Rabbit Ears update from the store shows up in SnapDock right away.
The TV icon comes from the installed Rabbit Ears app, so a new Rabbit Ears logo appears on the dock with its update.
No Rabbit Ears? The TV button still opens SnapDock's built-in TV, as before.

changelog.title: Rebuilt from scratch: Mac and Windows styles, Launchpad, Task Manager, Shortcuts
items: A brand-new SnapDock, rewritten from scratch. It never edits your own settings files: it adds one line to Hyprland's settings, and uninstall takes it out again.
Coming from an older SnapDock? Everything it changed is put back first (your autostart, launchers and anything it took out), then 2.0 sets itself up.

Three dock styles: Mac (floating glass shelf, icons grow under the mouse, a dot under open apps), Windows (taskbar across the bottom with a Start button) and SnapDock (glass pill). Choose at the bottom of SnapDock Settings.
Launchpad: All apps opens a full-screen grid of every app, like a Mac. Type to search, Enter to open, right-click to keep an app in the dock. You can switch back to Omarchy's app menu.
Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc, or right-click the dock): every app with its CPU and memory use, End task and Force quit, plus a Processes tab.

Shortcuts: YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, X, Facebook, Threads, Bluesky, Reddit, Snapchat, Pinterest, LinkedIn, Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Grok, DeepSeek, Gmail, Proton Mail, Google Drive, Notion, Figma, GitHub, Google Maps, Google Photos, Spotify, YouTube Music, Netflix, Disney+ and Twitch. Turn each on or off.
Unlock the dock to drag icons into a new order, for apps and shortcuts.
Right-click any open app: Close, Close all windows, Force quit, plus its windows, new window, minimize, maximize, snap layouts, move to desktop 1-5 and keep in dock.
Menus, SnapDock Settings and Shortcuts close by themselves a moment after the mouse leaves them.
Window previews: point at an open app to see live pictures of its windows; click one to bring it forward or close it.

Screenshot button on the dock, now better: click it to pick an area, a window, the whole screen, or the whole screen in 3 seconds. Right-click it for the whole screen straight away. Super + Shift + S picks an area; Shift + Print takes the whole screen.
The same icons in every dock style for Files (a plain folder, never a Mac face) and for Rabbit Ears (its own icon from the Omarchy Store).
Screensaver button on the dock: starts the screensaver and locks the computer.
A Trash on the dock (right-click to empty it).
New glossy 3D icons for everything SnapDock adds, and a bolder Omarchy Store icon. The Mac and Windows styles also use Mac or Windows looking icons for your apps.
Drag to snap and drag to a desktop rewritten: it notices the drag more reliably, even with title bars.
Live TV, snap layouts, Super + arrows, Show desktop (Super + D), title bar buttons (browsers too) and screenshots carry on from before.

changelog.title: SnapDock’s own dock, Show desktop, title bars on browsers
items: A new dock, made by SnapDock (the old nwg-dock is no longer needed). Click an app: it opens. Click again while it’s in front: it minimizes. Click a minimized app: it comes straight back.
Apps with several windows: a click shows the list; if they’re all minimized, one click brings them all back. App names appear when you point at an icon, and dots show how many windows are open.
Right-click menu on every dock icon: its windows, New window, Minimize / Bring back, Maximize, Snap layouts, Move to desktop 1–5, Keep in dock / Remove from dock, Close.
Show desktop: the last button on the dock, or Super + D, sends every window on the desktop into the dock. Press again and they all come back.
Dock size: Small, Medium or Large (SnapDock → Dock → Size).
Auto-hide, like a Mac: the dock slides away and returns when the mouse touches the bottom of the screen; windows then use the whole screen (SnapDock → Dock → Auto-hide).
Browsers get the title bar too (Chromium, Firefox, Brave…) with ⧉ ⊞ — □ ✕. Turn it off in SnapDock → Title bars.
Fixed: Chromium pinned under a broken name by the old dock.
All new texts in the 33 languages.

changelog.title: Minimize and move to desktop
items: Minimize, like Windows: a new — button on every title bar hides the window. Its icon stays in the dock; click it and the window comes back exactly where it was, on the desktop it came from.
Super + Down minimizes a window that isn't snapped, just like Win + Down. On a snapped window it first puts it back the way it was; press it again to minimize.
Move a window to another desktop (the 1 2 3 4 5 at the top left) with the new ⧉ title bar button: click a number in the little card, or just type it.
Or drag a window toward the top left corner: numbered tiles appear under the desktop numbers. Let go over one and the window moves there, keeping its size. You stay where you are.
New in the menu: SnapDock → Snap layouts → Bring back all minimized windows.
Title bar, left to right: ⧉ desktops · ⊞ snap layouts · — minimize · □ maximize · ✕ close. SnapDock → Title bars turns them on or off.
Uninstall puts minimized windows back on their desktops first, so nothing stays hidden.
All new texts are translated into the 33 languages.
The Omarchy Store app now always recognises SnapDock, even if you installed it with the installer file, so it shows UPDATE and Remove for it.

changelog.title: SnapDock speaks your language
items: 33 languages: English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish, Icelandic, Turkish, Greek, Hungarian, Lithuanian, Irish, Catalan, Bosnian, Arabic, Urdu, Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Sinhala, Thai, Vietnamese, Filipino, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese and Uzbek.
Follows your computer's language automatically. Pick another one: SnapDock → Language.
Menus, messages, notifications, the snap layout picker, key names in Omarchy's key list, the backup note and the app launchers are all translated.
Your choice is kept after updates.

changelog.title: Backups and Check for problems
items: Before SnapDock changes anything, it saves your desktop settings to a backup file in Downloads.
Backup & restore menu: save your settings any time, and put any backup back.
Uninstall can put back your exact setup from before SnapDock.
Check for problems finds conflicts (two docks, settings errors, missing parts), saves a report and can repair.
Older Omarchy versions get a clear message instead of a half setup.

changelog.title: Windows-style snapping
items: Super + arrow keys snap like Win + arrows.
Drag a window to an edge or corner to snap it, with a see-through preview.
Snap layouts (Super + Z or ⊞ on the title bar) and Snap Assist.
